summary.text: Borno fought with heavy cavalry on the open plains of the Sahel: riders in quilted armour and mail, from a walled capital at Ngazargamu. In the 1570s Idris Alooma added Turkish muskets and Turkish instructors, among the first guns in the Central Sudan.

arms.text: Mounted armies were Borno’s strength; Dunama II is said to have commanded 40,000 horsemen.
Idris Alooma got Turkish muskets and Turkish instructors from the Ottoman Sultan in the 1570s.
Ngazargamu, the walled capital, from about 1472.
Vassal states and nomad allies supplied men.

record.text: Borno inflicted a crushing defeat on Kwararafa in the late 15th century.
Kwararafa invaded Borno and sacked Ngazargamu.
Fulani jihadists took and destroyed Ngazargamu; al-Kanemi then drove them back.
Rabih beat Borno’s armies and ruled from Dikwa.
